section_1.title: The Dimension Ladder: From Circles to Spheres
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of an n-sphere by progressing from 1D to 3D. Define a sphere as the set of all points at a fixed distance 'r' from a center. Review the Pythagorean theorem as the foundation for the distance formula in coordinate space.
section_1.example: A 'Pointy the Penguin' character slides along a 1D line (interval), draws a 2D circle on ice, and then blows a 3D soap bubble to show the progression of spatial freedom.

section_2.title: Generalizing the Equation
section_2.content: Transition from the 3D equation (x² + y² + z² = r²) to the general n-dimensional equation (∑xᵢ² = r²). Explain that while we cannot visualize 4D+, the algebra remains consistent. Introduce the distinction between the Sⁿ (the surface) and the Bⁿ (the solid ball).
section_2.example: An animated chalkboard showing 'x² + y² = r²' for a circle, then adding '+ z²' for a sphere, and finally adding '+ ... + xₙ²' with a glowing 'n' to represent the jump to hyperspace.

section_3.title: The Vanishing Volume Paradox
section_3.content: Discuss how the volume of a unit n-sphere changes as 'n' increases. Unlike intuition, the volume doesn't grow indefinitely; it peaks at n=5 and then rapidly approaches zero as dimensions go to infinity.
section_3.example: A bar chart animation showing volume values: n=2 (π ≈ 3.14), n=5 (peak ≈ 5.26), n=20 (nearly 0). A visual metaphor of a balloon 'deflating' mathematically as it enters higher dimensions.

section_4.title: The 'Crust' Phenomenon (Surface Concentration)
section_4.content: Explain the counter-intuitive fact that in high dimensions, almost all the volume of a sphere lies in a thin shell near the surface. Use the ratio of volumes between a sphere of radius R and R-ε to show that most 'mass' migrates to the boundary.
section_4.example: An orange where, in 3D, the peel is thin, but in 100D, the 'peel' contains 99.9% of the fruit, leaving the center effectively empty.

section_5.title: The Cube and the 'Hiding' Sphere
section_5.content: Present the classic 'sphere in a box' problem. In high dimensions, a sphere inscribed in a unit hypercube occupies a negligible fraction of the cube's volume, while the corners of the cube stretch incredibly far away.
section_5.example: A 'Robot Packer' tries to fit a ball inside a 10D box. While the ball touches all sides, the robot finds massive empty 'pockets' in the corners of the box that could hold more than the sphere itself.

section_6.title: Real-World Echoes: Why It Matters
section_6.content: Conclude by linking these geometric oddities to modern technology, specifically the 'Curse of Dimensionality' in Big Data and Machine Learning, and Error-Correcting Codes in telecommunications.
section_6.example: A digital stream of data being compressed into 'spheres of influence' to show how high-dimensional geometry keeps our Wi-Fi signals clear and our AI models accurate.

section_3.example: A bar chart animation showing volume values: n=2 (π ≈ 3.14), n=5 (peak ≈ 5.26), n=20 (nearly 0). A visual metaphor of a balloon 'deflating' mathematically as it enters higher dimensions.

section_4.title: The 'Crust' Phenomenon (Surface Concentration)
section_4.content: Explain the counter-intuitive fact that in high dimensions, almost all the volume of a sphere lies in a thin shell near the surface. Use the ratio of volumes between a sphere of radius R and R-ε to show that most 'mass' migrates to the boundary.
section_4.example: An orange where, in 3D, the peel is thin, but in 100D, the 'peel' contains 99.9% of the fruit, leaving the center effectively empty.

section_5.title: The Cube and the 'Hiding' Sphere
section_5.content: Present the classic 'sphere in a box' problem. In high dimensions, a sphere inscribed in a unit hypercube occupies a negligible fraction of the cube's volume, while the corners of the cube stretch incredibly far away.
section_5.example: A 'Robot Packer' tries to fit a ball inside a 10D box. While the ball touches all sides, the robot finds massive empty 'pockets' in the corners of the box that could hold more than the sphere itself.

section_6.title: Real-World Echoes: Why It Matters
section_6.content: Conclude by linking these geometric oddities to modern technology, specifically the 'Curse of Dimensionality' in Big Data and Machine Learning, and Error-Correcting Codes in telecommunications.
section_6.example: A digital stream of data being compressed into 'spheres of influence' to show how high-dimensional geometry keeps our Wi-Fi signals clear and our AI models accurate.

section_2.example: An animated chalkboard showing 'x² + y² = r²' for a circle, then adding '+ z²' for a sphere, and finally adding '+ ... + xₙ²' with a glowing 'n' to represent the jump to hyperspace.

outline.title: Generalizing the Equation
outline.content: Transition from the 3D equation (x² + y² + z² = r²) to the general n-dimensional equation (∑xᵢ² = r²). Explain that while we cannot visualize 4D+, the algebra remains consistent. Introduce the distinction between the Sⁿ (the surface) and the Bⁿ (the solid ball).
outline.example: An animated chalkboard showing 'x² + y² = r²' for a circle, then adding '+ z²' for a sphere, and finally adding '+ ... + xₙ²' with a glowing 'n' to represent the jump to hyperspace.

outline.title: The Vanishing Volume Paradox
outline.content: Discuss how the volume of a unit n-sphere changes as 'n' increases. Unlike intuition, the volume doesn't grow indefinitely; it peaks at n=5 and then rapidly approaches zero as dimensions go to infinity.
outline.example: A bar chart animation showing volume values: n=2 (π ≈ 3.14), n=5 (peak ≈ 5.26), n=20 (nearly 0). A visual metaphor of a balloon 'deflating' mathematically as it enters higher dimensions.

storyboard.title: Generalizing the Equation

S-n represents the surface of the n-sphere.

Mathematical logic works where our visualization fails.

storyboard.title: The Vanishing Volume Paradox
lecture_lines: Intuition suggests volume grows with more dimensions.
Surprisingly, n-sphere volume peaks at dimension five.
Beyond five dimensions, the volume begins to shrink.
As dimensions increase, the volume rapidly approaches zero.
This is known as the vanishing volume paradox.

Bars grow for n=1 to 5. Bar for n=5 is tallest, color #FFFF00.
Bars for n=6 to n=20 rapidly shrink toward the X-axis.
A 3D sphere #00CCFF slowly shrinks in scale while its label 'n to infinity' glows brighter.
Text 'Volume to 0' appears in large bold font #FF4444.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Echoes: Why It Matters", [
            "High-dimensional geometry shapes modern big data.",
            "These concepts help refine error-correcting communication codes.",
            "Abstract math keeps our digital world connected."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Binary stream data
        binary_chars = "0110101011001"
        binary_vgroup = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=24, color="#00FF00") for char in binary_chars])
        binary_vgroup.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        # Position at the top of the grid area
        self.place_in_area(binary_vgroup, "A1", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Initial mask or clipping for a "flowing" effect
        stream_center = binary_vgroup.get_center()
        
        # Animation: binary stream sliding
        self.play(Write(binary_vgroup))
        self.play(binary_vgroup.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.5), rate_func=linear, run_time=2)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE) # Choosing a complementary color for points
        
        # Data points clustering into "spheres"
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.05, color=BLUE_A) for _ in range(30)])
        # Randomly scatter points in B1-D6
        area_tl = self.grid["B1"]
        area_br = self.grid["D6"]
        for p in points:
            p.move_to([
                np.random.uniform(area_tl[0], area_br[0]),
                np.random.uniform(area_br[1], area_tl[1]),
                0
            ])
            
        self.play(FadeIn(points))
        
        # Define cluster centers
        center1 = self.grid["C2"]
        center2 = self.grid["C5"]
        
        # "Spheres of influence" (Circles)
        sphere1 = Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE, stroke_width=2).move_to(center1)
        sphere2 = Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE, stroke_width=2).move_to(center2)
        
        # Animations: Points move to clusters and spheres appear
        self.play(
            *[points[i].animate.move_to(center1 + np.random.normal(0, 0.3, 3) * [1,1,0]) for i in range(15)],
            *[points[i].animate.move_to(center2 + np.random.normal(0, 0.3, 3) * [1,1,0]) for i in range(15, 30)],
            Create(sphere1),
            Create(sphere2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # Wi-Fi Icon
        wifi_dot = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.1)
        wifi_arc1 = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=45*DEGREES, angle=90*DEGREES, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        wifi_arc2 = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=45*DEGREES, angle=90*DEGREES, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        wifi_arc3 = Arc(radius=0.7, start_angle=45*DEGREES, angle=90*DEGREES, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        
        wifi_icon = VGroup(wifi_dot, wifi_arc1, wifi_arc2, wifi_arc3)
        self.place_in_area(wifi_icon, "E3", "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Fade out previous visuals and show Wi-Fi
        self.play(
            FadeOut(binary_vgroup),
            FadeOut(points),
            FadeOut(sphere1),
            FadeOut(sphere2),

lecture_lines: Imagine moving from one dimension to three.
A circle is points at distance 'r' in 2D.
A sphere extends this concept to 3D space.
The distance formula is the heart of these shapes.
All spheres share this fundamental geometric definition.
Start with the equation for a circle or sphere.
Extend the variables to describe an n-dimensional hypersphere.
We distinguish between the surface and the solid ball.
Intuition suggests volume grows with more dimensions.
Surprisingly, n-sphere volume peaks at dimension five.
Beyond five dimensions, the volume begins to shrink.
As dimensions increase, the volume rapidly approaches zero.
This is known as the vanishing volume paradox.
High-dimensional spheres are mostly made of crust.
Almost all volume lies near the outer surface.
The interior of the sphere is effectively empty.
Inscribe a sphere inside a unit hypercube.
In three dimensions, the sphere fills most space.
As dimensions grow, the cube's corners stretch away.
The sphere's volume becomes negligible in hyperspace.
Large empty pockets develop in the cube's corners.
High-dimensional geometry shapes modern big data.
These concepts refine error-correcting communication codes.
Abstract math keeps our digital world connected.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Vanishing Volume Paradox"
        lines = [
            "Intuition suggests volume grows with more dimensions.",
            "Surprisingly, n-sphere volume peaks at dimension five.",
            "Beyond five dimensions, the volume begins to shrink.",
            "As dimensions increase, the volume rapidly approaches zero.",
            "This is known as the vanishing volume paradox."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Pre-calculated unit n-sphere volumes for n=1 to 20
        volumes = [
            2.0, 3.14159, 4.18879, 4.93480, 5.26379, 
            5.16771, 4.72477, 4.05871, 3.29851, 2.55016, 
            1.88410, 1.33526, 0.91063, 0.59926, 0.38144, 
            0.23533, 0.14098, 0.08215, 0.04662, 0.02580
        ]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Intuition suggests volume grows with more dimensions.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 21, 5],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            axis_config={"color": "#BBBBBB"},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=3,
            tips=False
        )
        x_label = Text("Dimensions (n)", font_size=16, color="#BBBBBB")
        y_label = Text("Volume (V)", font_size=16, color="#BBBBBB")
        
        chart_group = VGroup(axes, x_label, y_label)
        self.place_in_area(chart_group, "A1", "D6")
        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT, buff=0.2).rotate(90*DEGREES)
        
        bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(5):
            # Map volume to bar height relative to axis scale
            bar_height = volumes[i] * (axes.y_length / 6)
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.12,
                height=bar_height,
                fill_color=BLUE,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i+1, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            bars.add(bar)
            
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        self.play(Create(bars), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Surprisingly, n-sphere volume peaks at dimension five.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Highlight the 5th bar (n=5)
        self.play(bars[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00").set_fill(opacity=1))
        peak_label = Text("Peak: n=5", font_size=14, color="#FFFF00")
        peak_label.next_to(bars[4], UP, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Write(peak_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Beyond five dimensions, the volume begins to shrink.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        shrink_bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(5, 10):
            bar_height = volumes[i] * (axes.y_length / 6)
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.12,
                height=bar_height,
                fill_color=BLUE_E,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i+1, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            shrink_bars.add(bar)
            
        self.play(Create(shrink_bars), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # As dimensions increase, the volume rapidly approaches zero.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        zero_bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(10, 20):
            bar_height = volumes[i] * (axes.y_length / 6)
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.12,
                height=bar_height,
                fill_color=DARK_GREY,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i+1, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            zero_bars.add(bar)
            
        self.play(Create(zero_bars), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Representing a 3D sphere that shrinks
        sphere_repr = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#00CCFF", fill_opacity=0.8)
        inner_highlight = Circle(radius=0.08, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(sphere_repr.get_center() + UP*0.15 + LEFT*0.15)
        sphere_group = VGroup(sphere_repr, inner_highlight)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sphere_group, "E4")
        inf_label = Text("n → ∞", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        inf_label.next_to(sphere_group, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere_group), Write(inf_label))
        self.play(
            sphere_group.animate.scale(0.05),
            inf_label.animate.set_color(YELLOW).scale(1.2),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This is known as the vanishing volume paradox.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        paradox_text = Text("Volume to 0", font_size=32, color="#FF4444", weight=BOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(paradox_text, "F4")
        
        self.play(Write(paradox_text))
        self.wait(2)

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)

        # Data from storyboard and script

            "- Almost all volume lies near the outer surface.",
            "- The interior of the sphere is effectively empty."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        ORANGE_COLOR = "#FFA500"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        annulus_initial = Annulus(inner_radius=1.6, outer_radius=1.8, color=ORANGE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=0)

        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The 'Crust' Phenomenon (Surface Concentration)
outline.content: Explain the counter-intuitive fact that in high dimensions, almost all the volume of a sphere lies in a thin shell near the surface. Use the ratio of volumes between a sphere of radius R and R-ε to show that most 'mass' migrates to the boundary.
outline.example: An orange where, in 3D, the peel is thin, but in 100D, the 'peel' contains 99.9% of the fruit, leaving the center effectively empty.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard and script
        title = "The 'Crust' Phenomenon"
        lines = [
            "- High-dimensional spheres are mostly made of crust.",
            "- Almost all volume lies near the outer surface.",
            "- The interior of the sphere is effectively empty."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        ORANGE_COLOR = "#FFA500"
        
        # Assets
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg]
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/orange.svg]
        sphere_asset_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg"
        orange_asset_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/orange.svg"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR))
        
        # A circle with a shaded outer ring (thickness epsilon). Outer ring color #FFA500.
        circle_outline = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        # Using a persistent Annulus and updating it via become or updater to avoid overhead
        crust_2d = Annulus(inner_radius=1.3, outer_radius=1.5, color=ORANGE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=0)
        
        viz_group = VGroup(crust_2d, circle_outline)
        self.place_in_area(viz_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        center_point = viz_group.get_center()
        
        self.play(Create(circle_outline), FadeIn(crust_2d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR))
        
        # 3D sphere [Asset: sphere.svg] with a shell. The inner core shrinks as n increases.
        sphere_svg = SVGMobject(sphere_asset_path).scale(1.5).move_to(center_point)
        sphere_svg.set_color(WHITE).set_opacity(0.3)
        
        # We'll simulate the "shrinking core" using a white circle on top of an orange circle
        shell_bg = Circle(radius=1.5, color=ORANGE_COLOR, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0).move_to(center_point)
        core_white = Circle(radius=1.3, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0).move_to(center_point)
        
        n_tracker = ValueTracker(2)
        # Radius of core = 1.5 * (0.96)^n
        # Instead of always_redraw, use an updater on the core_white circle
        def core_updater(m):
            n = n_tracker.get_value()
            new_radius = 1.5 * (0.95 ** (n/2)) # Heuristic for shrinking
            # Manim's scale is relative, so we use scale_to_fit_width
            m.scale_to_fit_width(max(0.01, 2 * new_radius))
            m.move_to(center_point)

        core_white.add_updater(core_updater)
        
        # Progress indicator for dimension n
        n_label = Text("n = ", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        n_val = Integer(2, font_size=24, color=WHITE).next_to(n_label, RIGHT)
        n_group = VGroup(n_label, n_val)
        self.place_at_grid(n_group, "B3")
        n_val.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_value(int(n_tracker.get_value())))

        # Transition to SVG view
        self.play(
            FadeOut(crust_2d),
            FadeIn(shell_bg),
            FadeIn(core_white),
            FadeIn(sphere_svg),
            FadeIn(n_group)
        )
        
        # n increases from 2 to 100
        # Reduced run_time slightly to save on render time, but keep it smooth
        self.play(n_tracker.animate.set_value(100), run_time=4, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR))
        
        # For n=100, the sphere is orange [Asset: orange.svg] #FFA500 except for a tiny white dot in the center.
        orange_svg = SVGMobject(orange_asset_path).scale(1.5).move_to(center_point)
        orange_svg.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR)
        
        center_dot = Dot(center_point, radius=0.03, color=WHITE)
        label_empty = Text("Mostly empty interior", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_empty, "E4")
        arrow = Arrow(start=label_empty.get_left(), end=center_point, buff=0.1, color=WHITE)

        # Clean up previous updaters and mobjects
        core_white.remove_updater(core_updater)
        n_val.clear_updaters()
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(shell_bg),
            FadeOut(core_white),
            FadeOut(sphere_svg),
            FadeIn(orange_svg),
            FadeIn(center_dot),
            Create(arrow),
            FadeIn(label_empty)
        )
        
        self.play(n_val.animate.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR))
        self.wait(2)

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

section_1.title: The Dimension Ladder: From Circles to Spheres
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of an n-sphere by progressing from 1D to 3D. Define a sphere as the set of all points at a fixed distance 'r' from a center. Review the Pythagorean theorem as the foundation for the distance formula in coordinate space.
section_1.example: A 'Pointy the Penguin' character slides along a 1D line (interval), draws a 2D circle on ice, and then blows a 3D soap bubble to show the progression of spatial freedom.

section_2.title: Generalizing the Equation
section_2.content: Transition from the 3D equation (x² + y² + z² = r²) to the general n-dimensional equation (∑xᵢ² = r²). Explain that while we cannot visualize 4D+, the algebra remains consistent. Introduce the distinction between the Sⁿ (the surface) and the Bⁿ (the solid ball).
section_2.example: An animated chalkboard showing 'x² + y² = r²' for a circle, then adding '+ z²' for a sphere, and finally adding '+ ... + xₙ²' with a glowing 'n' to represent the jump to hyperspace.

section_3.title: The Vanishing Volume Paradox
section_3.content: Discuss how the volume of a unit n-sphere changes as 'n' increases. Unlike intuition, the volume doesn't grow indefinitely; it peaks at n=5 and then rapidly approaches zero as dimensions go to infinity.
section_3.example: A bar chart animation showing volume values: n=2 (π ≈ 3.14), n=5 (peak ≈ 5.26), n=20 (nearly 0). A visual metaphor of a balloon 'deflating' mathematically as it enters higher dimensions.

section_4.title: The 'Crust' Phenomenon (Surface Concentration)
section_4.content: Explain the counter-intuitive fact that in high dimensions, almost all the volume of a sphere lies in a thin shell near the surface. Use the ratio of volumes between a sphere of radius R and R-ε to show that most 'mass' migrates to the boundary.
section_4.example: An orange where, in 3D, the peel is thin, but in 100D, the 'peel' contains 99.9% of the fruit, leaving the center effectively empty.

section_5.title: The Cube and the 'Hiding' Sphere
section_5.content: Present the classic 'sphere in a box' problem. In high dimensions, a sphere inscribed in a unit hypercube occupies a negligible fraction of the cube's volume, while the corners of the cube stretch incredibly far away.
section_5.example: A 'Robot Packer' tries to fit a ball inside a 10D box. While the ball touches all sides, the robot finds massive empty 'pockets' in the corners of the box that could hold more than the sphere itself.

section_6.title: Real-World Echoes: Why It Matters
section_6.content: Conclude by linking these geometric oddities to modern technology, specifically the 'Curse of Dimensionality' in Big Data and Machine Learning, and Error-Correcting Codes in telecommunications.
section_6.example: A digital stream of data being compressed into 'spheres of influence' to show how high-dimensional geometry keeps our Wi-Fi signals clear and our AI models accurate.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        title = "The Vanishing Volume Paradox"
        lines = [
            "Intuition suggests volume grows with more dimensions.",
            "Surprisingly, n-sphere volume peaks at dimension five.",
            "Beyond five dimensions, the volume begins to shrink.",
            "As dimensions increase, the volume rapidly approaches zero.",
            "This is known as the vanishing volume paradox."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Pre-calculated unit n-sphere volumes for n=1 to 20
        volumes = [
            2.0, 3.14159, 4.18879, 4.93480, 5.26379, 
            5.16771, 4.72477, 4.05871, 3.29851, 2.55016, 
            1.88410, 1.33526, 0.91063, 0.59926, 0.38144, 
            0.23533, 0.14098, 0.08215, 0.04662, 0.02580
        ]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Intuition suggests volume grows with more dimensions.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 21, 5],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            axis_config={"color": "#BBBBBB"},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=3,
            tips=False
        )
        x_label = Text("Dimensions (n)", font_size=16, color="#BBBBBB")
        y_label = Text("Volume (V)", font_size=16, color="#BBBBBB")
        
        chart_group = VGroup(axes, x_label, y_label)
        self.place_in_area(chart_group, "A1", "D6")
        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT, buff=0.2).rotate(90*DEGREES)
        
        bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(5):
            # Map volume to bar height relative to axis scale
            bar_height = volumes[i] * (axes.y_length / 6)
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.12,
                height=bar_height,
                fill_color=BLUE,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i+1, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            bars.add(bar)
            
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        self.play(Create(bars), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Surprisingly, n-sphere volume peaks at dimension five.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Highlight the 5th bar (n=5)
        self.play(bars[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00").set_fill(opacity=1))
        peak_label = Text("Peak: n=5", font_size=14, color="#FFFF00")
        peak_label.next_to(bars[4], UP, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Write(peak_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Beyond five dimensions, the volume begins to shrink.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        shrink_bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(5, 10):
            bar_height = volumes[i] * (axes.y_length / 6)
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.12,
                height=bar_height,
                fill_color=BLUE_E,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i+1, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            shrink_bars.add(bar)
            
        self.play(Create(shrink_bars), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # As dimensions increase, the volume rapidly approaches zero.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        zero_bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(10, 20):
            bar_height = volumes[i] * (axes.y_length / 6)
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.12,
                height=bar_height,
                fill_color=DARK_GREY,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i+1, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            zero_bars.add(bar)
            
        self.play(Create(zero_bars), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Representing a 3D sphere that shrinks
        sphere_repr = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#00CCFF", fill_opacity=0.8)
        inner_highlight = Circle(radius=0.08, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(sphere_repr.get_center() + UP*0.15 + LEFT*0.15)
        sphere_group = VGroup(sphere_repr, inner_highlight)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sphere_group, "E4")
        inf_label = Text("n → ∞", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        inf_label.next_to(sphere_group, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere_group), Write(inf_label))
        self.play(
            sphere_group.animate.scale(0.05),
            inf_label.animate.set_color(YELLOW).scale(1.2),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This is known as the vanishing volume paradox.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        paradox_text = Text("Volume to 0", font_size=32, color="#FF4444", weight=BOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(paradox_text, "F4")

        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard and script
        title = "The 'Crust' Phenomenon"
        lines = [
            "- High-dimensional spheres are mostly made of crust.",
            "- Almost all volume lies near the outer surface.",
            "- The interior of the sphere is effectively empty."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        ORANGE_COLOR = "#FFA500"
        
        # Assets
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg]
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/orange.svg]
        sphere_asset_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg"
        orange_asset_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/orange.svg"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR))
        
        # A circle with a shaded outer ring (thickness epsilon). Outer ring color #FFA500.
        circle_outline = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        # Using a persistent Annulus and updating it via become or updater to avoid overhead
        crust_2d = Annulus(inner_radius=1.3, outer_radius=1.5, color=ORANGE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=0)
        
        viz_group = VGroup(crust_2d, circle_outline)
        self.place_in_area(viz_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        center_point = viz_group.get_center()
        
        self.play(Create(circle_outline), FadeIn(crust_2d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR))
        
        # 3D sphere [Asset: sphere.svg] with a shell. The inner core shrinks as n increases.
        sphere_svg = SVGMobject(sphere_asset_path).scale(1.5).move_to(center_point)
        sphere_svg.set_color(WHITE).set_opacity(0.3)
        
        # We'll simulate the "shrinking core" using a white circle on top of an orange circle
        shell_bg = Circle(radius=1.5, color=ORANGE_COLOR, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0).move_to(center_point)
        core_white = Circle(radius=1.3, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0).move_to(center_point)
        
        n_tracker = ValueTracker(2)
        # Radius of core = 1.5 * (0.96)^n
        # Instead of always_redraw, use an updater on the core_white circle
        def core_updater(m):
            n = n_tracker.get_value()
            new_radius = 1.5 * (0.95 ** (n/2)) # Heuristic for shrinking
            # Manim's scale is relative, so we use scale_to_fit_width
            m.scale_to_fit_width(max(0.01, 2 * new_radius))
            m.move_to(center_point)

        core_white.add_updater(core_updater)
        
        # Progress indicator for dimension n
        n_label = Text("n = ", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        n_val = Integer(2, font_size=24, color=WHITE).next_to(n_label, RIGHT)
        n_group = VGroup(n_label, n_val)
        self.place_at_grid(n_group, "B3")
        n_val.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_value(int(n_tracker.get_value())))

        # Transition to SVG view
        self.play(
            FadeOut(crust_2d),
            FadeIn(shell_bg),
            FadeIn(core_white),
            FadeIn(sphere_svg),
            FadeIn(n_group)
        )
        
        # n increases from 2 to 100
        # Reduced run_time slightly to save on render time, but keep it smooth
        self.play(n_tracker.animate.set_value(100), run_time=4, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR))
        
        # For n=100, the sphere is orange [Asset: orange.svg] #FFA500 except for a tiny white dot in the center.
        orange_svg = SVGMobject(orange_asset_path).scale(1.5).move_to(center_point)
        orange_svg.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR)
        
        center_dot = Dot(center_point, radius=0.03, color=WHITE)
        label_empty = Text("Mostly empty interior", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_empty, "E4")
        arrow = Arrow(start=label_empty.get_left(), end=center_point, buff=0.1, color=WHITE)

        # Clean up previous updaters and mobjects
        core_white.remove_updater(core_updater)
        n_val.clear_updaters()
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(shell_bg),
            FadeOut(core_white),
            FadeOut(sphere_svg),
            FadeIn(orange_svg),
            FadeIn(center_dot),
            Create(arrow),
            FadeIn(label_empty)
        )
        
        self.play(n_val.animate.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Echoes: Why It Matters", [
            "High-dimensional geometry shapes modern big data.",
            "These concepts help refine error-correcting communication codes.",
            "Abstract math keeps our digital world connected."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Binary stream data
        binary_chars = "0110101011001"
        binary_vgroup = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=24, color="#00FF00") for char in binary_chars])
        binary_vgroup.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        # Position at the top of the grid area
        self.place_in_area(binary_vgroup, "A1", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Initial mask or clipping for a "flowing" effect
        stream_center = binary_vgroup.get_center()
        
        # Animation: binary stream sliding
        self.play(Write(binary_vgroup))
        self.play(binary_vgroup.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.5), rate_func=linear, run_time=2)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE) # Choosing a complementary color for points
        
        # Data points clustering into "spheres"
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.05, color=BLUE_A) for _ in range(30)])
        # Randomly scatter points in B1-D6
        area_tl = self.grid["B1"]
        area_br = self.grid["D6"]
        for p in points:
            p.move_to([
                np.random.uniform(area_tl[0], area_br[0]),
                np.random.uniform(area_br[1], area_tl[1]),
                0
            ])
            
        self.play(FadeIn(points))
        
        # Define cluster centers
        center1 = self.grid["C2"]
        center2 = self.grid["C5"]
        
        # "Spheres of influence" (Circles)
        sphere1 = Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE, stroke_width=2).move_to(center1)
        sphere2 = Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE, stroke_width=2).move_to(center2)
        
        # Animations: Points move to clusters and spheres appear
        self.play(
            *[points[i].animate.move_to(center1 + np.random.normal(0, 0.3, 3) * [1,1,0]) for i in range(15)],
            *[points[i].animate.move_to(center2 + np.random.normal(0, 0.3, 3) * [1,1,0]) for i in range(15, 30)],
            Create(sphere1),
            Create(sphere2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # Wi-Fi Icon
        wifi_dot = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.1)
        wifi_arc1 = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=45*DEGREES, angle=90*DEGREES, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        wifi_arc2 = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=45*DEGREES, angle=90*DEGREES, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        wifi_arc3 = Arc(radius=0.7, start_angle=45*DEGREES, angle=90*DEGREES, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        
        wifi_icon = VGroup(wifi_dot, wifi_arc1, wifi_arc2, wifi_arc3)
        self.place_in_area(wifi_icon, "E3", "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Fade out previous visuals and show Wi-Fi
        self.play(
            FadeOut(binary_vgroup),
            FadeOut(points),
            FadeOut(sphere1),
            FadeOut(sphere2),
            FadeIn(wifi_icon)
        )
        
        # Pulse animation
        self.play(
            wifi_icon.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            wifi_icon.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Echoes: Why It Matters", [
            "High-dimensional geometry shapes modern big data.",
            "These concepts help refine error-correcting communication codes.",
            "Abstract math keeps our digital world connected."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Binary stream data
        binary_chars = "0110101011001"
        binary_vgroup = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=24, color="#00FF00") for char in binary_chars])
        binary_vgroup.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        # Position at the top of the grid area
        self.place_in_area(binary_vgroup, "A1", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Initial mask or clipping for a "flowing" effect
        stream_center = binary_vgroup.get_center()
        
        # Animation: binary stream sliding
        self.play(Write(binary_vgroup))
        self.play(binary_vgroup.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.5), rate_func=linear, run_time=2)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE) # Choosing a complementary color for points
        
        # Data points clustering into "spheres"
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.05, color=BLUE_A) for _ in range(30)])
        # Randomly scatter points in B1-D6
        area_tl = self.grid["B1"]
        area_br = self.grid["D6"]
        for p in points:
            p.move_to([
                np.random.uniform(area_tl[0], area_br[0]),
                np.random.uniform(area_br[1], area_tl[1]),
                0
            ])
            
        self.play(FadeIn(points))
        
        # Define cluster centers
        center1 = self.grid["C2"]
        center2 = self.grid["C5"]
        
        # "Spheres of influence" (Circles)
        sphere1 = Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE, stroke_width=2).move_to(center1)
        sphere2 = Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE, stroke_width=2).move_to(center2)
        
        # Animations: Points move to clusters and spheres appear
        self.play(
            *[points[i].animate.move_to(center1 + np.random.normal(0, 0.3, 3) * [1,1,0]) for i in range(15)],
            *[points[i].animate.move_to(center2 + np.random.normal(0, 0.3, 3) * [1,1,0]) for i in range(15, 30)],
            Create(sphere1),
            Create(sphere2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # Wi-Fi Icon
        wifi_dot = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.1)
        wifi_arc1 = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=45*DEGREES, angle=90*DEGREES, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        wifi_arc2 = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=45*DEGREES, angle=90*DEGREES, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        wifi_arc3 = Arc(radius=0.7, start_angle=45*DEGREES, angle=90*DEGREES, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        
        wifi_icon = VGroup(wifi_dot, wifi_arc1, wifi_arc2, wifi_arc3)
        self.place_in_area(wifi_icon, "E3", "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Fade out previous visuals and show Wi-Fi
        self.play(
            FadeOut(binary_vgroup),
            FadeOut(points),
            FadeOut(sphere1),
            FadeOut(sphere2),
            FadeIn(wifi_icon)
        )
        
        # Pulse animation
        self.play(
            wifi_icon.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            wifi_icon.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Generalizing the Equation
outline.content: Transition from the 3D equation (x² + y² + z² = r²) to the general n-dimensional equation (∑xᵢ² = r²). Explain that while we cannot visualize 4D+, the algebra remains consistent. Introduce the distinction between the Sⁿ (the surface) and the Bⁿ (the solid ball).
outline.example: An animated chalkboard showing 'x² + y² = r²' for a circle, then adding '+ z²' for a sphere, and finally adding '+ ... + xₙ²' with a glowing 'n' to represent the jump to hyperspace.

Symbol B^n appears. Solid ball interior flashes #FF0000.
Text 'Logic' #FFFFFF appears as formulas fade.

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        lecture_lines = [
            "We can extend the 3D equation to n-dimensions.",
            "The algebra remains consistent beyond three dimensions.",
            "S-n represents the surface of the n-sphere.",
            "B-n refers to the solid n-dimensional ball.",
            "Mathematical logic works where our visualization fails."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Generalizing the Equation", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualizing the 2D case first
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        eq2d = MathTex("x^2 + y^2 = r^2", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(eq2d, 'C2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(eq2d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Generalizing to 3D
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        eq3d = MathTex("x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = r^2", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(eq3d, 'C2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Transform(eq2d, eq3d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Moving to n-dimensions and labeling the surface S^n
        # Matching Green color #00FF00
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        eqnd = MathTex("x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \dots + x_n^2 = r^2", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(eqnd, 'C2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        sn_label = MathTex("S^n", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(sn_label, 'B4', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(eq2d, eqnd),
            FadeIn(sn_label)
        )
        self.play(Indicate(sn_label, color="#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Introducing the ball B^n
        # Matching Red color #FF0000
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        bn_label = MathTex("B^n", color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(bn_label, 'D4', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bn_label))
        self.play(Indicate(bn_label, color="#FF0000"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Highlighting the 'n' to emphasize the jump to hyperspace
        # Matching Magenta color #FF00FF
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        # Highlighting the 'n' index in the generalized equation
        # Manual placement of high-light circle
        n_highlight = Circle(radius=0.35, color="#FF00FF").set_stroke(width=5)
        self.place_at_grid(n_highlight, 'C4')
        n_highlight.shift(RIGHT * 1.1 + DOWN * 0.1) # Center on 'n'
        
        self.play(Create(n_highlight))
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(n_highlight.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=0.4)
            self.play(n_highlight.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=0.4)
        
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard and script
        title = "The 'Crust' Phenomenon"
        lines = [
            "- High-dimensional spheres are mostly made of crust.",
            "- Almost all volume lies near the outer surface.",
            "- The interior of the sphere is effectively empty."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        ORANGE_COLOR = "#FFA500"
        
        # Assets
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg]
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/orange.svg]
        sphere_asset_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg"
        orange_asset_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/orange.svg"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR))
        
        # A circle with a shaded outer ring (thickness epsilon). Outer ring color #FFA500.
        circle_outline = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        # Using a persistent Annulus and updating it via become or updater to avoid overhead
        crust_2d = Annulus(inner_radius=1.3, outer_radius=1.5, color=ORANGE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=0)
        
        viz_group = VGroup(crust_2d, circle_outline)
        self.place_in_area(viz_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        center_point = viz_group.get_center()
        
        self.play(Create(circle_outline), FadeIn(crust_2d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR))
        
        # 3D sphere [Asset: sphere.svg] with a shell. The inner core shrinks as n increases.
        sphere_svg = SVGMobject(sphere_asset_path).scale(1.5).move_to(center_point)
        sphere_svg.set_color(WHITE).set_opacity(0.3)
        
        # We'll simulate the "shrinking core" using a white circle on top of an orange circle
        shell_bg = Circle(radius=1.5, color=ORANGE_COLOR, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0).move_to(center_point)
        core_white = Circle(radius=1.3, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0).move_to(center_point)
        
        n_tracker = ValueTracker(2)
        # Radius of core = 1.5 * (0.96)^n
        # Instead of always_redraw, use an updater on the core_white circle
        def core_updater(m):
            n = n_tracker.get_value()
            new_radius = 1.5 * (0.95 ** (n/2)) # Heuristic for shrinking
            # Manim's scale is relative, so we use scale_to_fit_width
            m.scale_to_fit_width(max(0.01, 2 * new_radius))
            m.move_to(center_point)

        core_white.add_updater(core_updater)
        
        # Progress indicator for dimension n
        n_label = Text("n = ", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        n_val = Integer(2, font_size=24, color=WHITE).next_to(n_label, RIGHT)
        n_group = VGroup(n_label, n_val)
        self.place_at_grid(n_group, "B3")
        n_val.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_value(int(n_tracker.get_value())))

        # Transition to SVG view
        self.play(
            FadeOut(crust_2d),
            FadeIn(shell_bg),
            FadeIn(core_white),
            FadeIn(sphere_svg),
            FadeIn(n_group)
        )
        
        # n increases from 2 to 100
        # Reduced run_time slightly to save on render time, but keep it smooth
        self.play(n_tracker.animate.set_value(100), run_time=4, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR))
        
        # For n=100, the sphere is orange [Asset: orange.svg] #FFA500 except for a tiny white dot in the center.
        orange_svg = SVGMobject(orange_asset_path).scale(1.5).move_to(center_point)
        orange_svg.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR)
        
        center_dot = Dot(center_point, radius=0.03, color=WHITE)
        label_empty = Text("Mostly empty interior", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_empty, "E4")
        arrow = Arrow(start=label_empty.get_left(), end=center_point, buff=0.1, color=WHITE)

        # Clean up previous updaters and mobjects
        core_white.remove_updater(core_updater)
        n_val.clear_updaters()
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(shell_bg),
            FadeOut(core_white),
            FadeOut(sphere_svg),
            FadeIn(orange_svg),
            FadeIn(center_dot),
            Create(arrow),
            FadeIn(label_empty)
        )
        
        self.play(n_val.animate.set_color(ORANGE_COLOR))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Vanishing Volume Paradox
outline.content: Discuss how the volume of a unit n-sphere changes as 'n' increases. Unlike intuition, the volume doesn't grow indefinitely; it peaks at n=5 and then rapidly approaches zero as dimensions go to infinity.

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Vanishing Volume Paradox"
        lines = [
            "Intuition suggests volume grows with more dimensions.",
            "Surprisingly, n-sphere volume peaks at dimension five.",
            "Beyond five dimensions, the volume begins to shrink.",
            "As dimensions increase, the volume rapidly approaches zero.",
            "This is known as the vanishing volume paradox."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Pre-calculated unit n-sphere volumes for n=1 to 20
        volumes = [
            2.0, 3.14159, 4.18879, 4.93480, 5.26379, 
            5.16771, 4.72477, 4.05871, 3.29851, 2.55016, 
            1.88410, 1.33526, 0.91063, 0.59926, 0.38144, 
            0.23533, 0.14098, 0.08215, 0.04662, 0.02580
        ]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Intuition suggests volume grows with more dimensions.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 21, 5],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            axis_config={"color": "#BBBBBB"},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=3,
            tips=False
        )
        x_label = Text("Dimensions (n)", font_size=16, color="#BBBBBB")
        y_label = Text("Volume (V)", font_size=16, color="#BBBBBB")
        
        chart_group = VGroup(axes, x_label, y_label)
        self.place_in_area(chart_group, "A1", "D6")
        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT, buff=0.2).rotate(90*DEGREES)
        
        bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(5):
            # Map volume to bar height relative to axis scale
            bar_height = volumes[i] * (axes.y_length / 6)
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.12,
                height=bar_height,
                fill_color=BLUE,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i+1, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            bars.add(bar)
            
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        self.play(Create(bars), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Surprisingly, n-sphere volume peaks at dimension five.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Highlight the 5th bar (n=5)
        self.play(bars[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00").set_fill(opacity=1))
        peak_label = Text("Peak: n=5", font_size=14, color="#FFFF00")
        peak_label.next_to(bars[4], UP, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Write(peak_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Beyond five dimensions, the volume begins to shrink.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        shrink_bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(5, 10):
            bar_height = volumes[i] * (axes.y_length / 6)
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.12,
                height=bar_height,
                fill_color=BLUE_E,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i+1, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            shrink_bars.add(bar)
            
        self.play(Create(shrink_bars), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # As dimensions increase, the volume rapidly approaches zero.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        zero_bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(10, 20):
            bar_height = volumes[i] * (axes.y_length / 6)
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=0.12,
                height=bar_height,
                fill_color=DARK_GREY,
                fill_opacity=0.8,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            bar.move_to(axes.c2p(i+1, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            zero_bars.add(bar)
            
        self.play(Create(zero_bars), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Representing a 3D sphere that shrinks
        sphere_repr = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#00CCFF", fill_opacity=0.8)
        inner_highlight = Circle(radius=0.08, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(sphere_repr.get_center() + UP*0.15 + LEFT*0.15)
        sphere_group = VGroup(sphere_repr, inner_highlight)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sphere_group, "E4")
        inf_label = Text("n → ∞", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        inf_label.next_to(sphere_group, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere_group), Write(inf_label))
        self.play(
            sphere_group.animate.scale(0.05),
            inf_label.animate.set_color(YELLOW).scale(1.2),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This is known as the vanishing volume paradox.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        paradox_text = Text("Volume to 0", font_size=32, color="#FF4444", weight=BOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(paradox_text, "F4")
        
        self.play(Write(paradox_text))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Dimension Ladder: From Circles to Spheres
outline.content: Introduce the concept of an n-sphere by progressing from 1D to 3D. Define a sphere as the set of all points at a fixed distance 'r' from a center. Review the Pythagorean theorem as the foundation for the distance formula in coordinate space.
outline.example: A 'Pointy the Penguin' character slides along a 1D line (interval), draws a 2D circle on ice, and then blows a 3D soap bubble to show the progression of spatial freedom.

storyboard.title: The Dimension Ladder: From Circles to Spheres
lecture_lines: Imagine moving from one dimension to three.
A circle is points at distance 'r' in 2D.
A sphere extends this concept to 3D space.
The distance formula is the heart of these shapes.
All spheres share this fundamental geometric definition.
animations: A point moves along a 1D line #FFFFFF, leaving a trail of length 2r. Label: '1D: Interval'.
The 1D line rotates 360 degrees in a 2D plane to form a circle with radius r. Label: '2D: Circle'.
The 2D circle rotates in 3D space to form a 3D sphere. Label: '3D: Sphere'.
Show the distance formula sqrt(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) = r next to the sphere. Formula color: #00FFFF.

Character 'Pointy' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pointy.svg] #FFD700 hops from the line, to the circle, then inside the bubble [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bubble.svg].

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
